clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 11093 state the order's subject, assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Administrator of General Services, and the authority under which the President acted, including Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958; they operate only through the numbered sections that follow, so they ended with the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 1 of EO 11093 directs the Administrator of General Services to prepare national emergency plans and develop preparedness programs designed to permit modification or expansion of the activities of the General Services Administration under the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949, as amended, and other statutes prescribing the Administrator's duties, and lists twelve subjects the plans and programs are to include, among them operation and protection of Federal buildings, public utilities service management, telecommunications, transportation management, records management, an emergency Federal Register, supply support, survival item stockpiles, a national industrial reserve, and administration and operation of the stockpile of strategic and critical materials. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 2 of EO 11093 assigns the Administrator functions, set out in lettered paragraphs on public buildings, public utility service management, communications, transportation, records, the Federal Register, claimancy, survival item stockpiles, the national industrial reserve and machine tool program, and excess and surplus real and personal property. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 3 of EO 11093 directs the Administrator, in consonance with the national civil defense plans, programs and operations of the Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, to carry out facilities protection and building and warden service functions and damage assessment. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 4 of EO 11093 directs the Administrator to assist the Office of Emergency Planning in formulating plans and programs relating to the certification of procurement programs, subsidy payments and plant improvement programs provided for by the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 5 of EO 11093 directs the Administrator to assist the Office of Emergency Planning in formulating plans, programs and reports relating to the stockpiling of strategic and critical materials, and, within those plans, to provide for procurement, storage, security, maintenance, inspection, withdrawal and disposal of materials, supplies and equipment. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 6 of EO 11093 directs the Administrator, within the framework of Federal research objectives, to conduct or supervise research directly concerned with carrying out emergency preparedness responsibilities, to designate representatives for necessary ad hoc or task force groups, and to provide advice and assistance to other agencies in planning for research in areas involving the Administrator's interest. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 7 of EO 11093 sets the guidance by which the Administrator, in carrying out the functions assigned in the order, is to be guided: interagency cooperation, Presidential coordination (the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning is to advise and assist the President in determining policy for the performance of functions under the order and in coordinating them with the total national preparedness program), and emergency planning (emergency plans, programs and organization are to be developed as an integral part of the continuing activities of the General Services Administration on the basis that it will have responsibility for carrying them out during an emergency, and the Administrator is to be prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under the order). It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 8 of EO 11093 directs the Administrator to provide appropriate participation in the national resources evaluation program administered by the Office of Emergency Planning. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 9 of EO 11093 provides that nothing in the order is to be construed as conferring authority under Title III of the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action prepared or developed pursuant to the order, and states that such authority is reserved to the President. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 10 of EO 11093 authorizes the Administrator to redelegate within the General Services Administration the functions assigned to him in the order. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (20), "Executive Order No. 11093 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 11 of EO 11093 provides that, to the extent of any inconsistency between the provisions of any prior order and the provisions of this order, the latter controls. That rule was a continuing command and stayed in force while the order did. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11093: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. research_rationale:
EO 11093 (1963-02-26; Assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Administrator of General Services) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (28 FR 1851, Federal Register of 1963-02-28), whose file also contains neighbouring material; the order was delimited by its heading and the John F. Kennedy signature line. The dossier's machine segmentation, which cuts sections into lettered fragments and repeats some, was replaced by 12 scopes: one for the enacting words and one for each numbered section. Its own terms contain no end date, expiry or termination condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, item (20), cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823; page record checked: heading, date and text hash agree with the held text) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register print of 34 FR 17567 onward (OCR text), which lists the same order. No amendment, suspension or other instrument naming it is held besides EO 11490, which revokes it. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog) are coverage statements read before use; they are leads, not independent review.

savings.reason: Item (20) of Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 revokes EO 11093. In the held American Presidency Project transcription, Sec. 3014 reads: "Except as provided by Section 3015, nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from any now existing assignment of functions to any department or agency or officer thereof made by statute, Executive order, or Presidential directives, including Memoranda." Because Sec. 3014 begins with that exception, it does not preserve the revoked order. The end source span cited for this claim runs from "SECTION 501. Functions." through Sec. 3015, that is Parts 5 through 30 of EO 11490. I read Sec. 3014 and Sec. 3015; I did not read the other Parts to decide whether any of them carries this order's commands forward, so no transfer or accrual is claimed and the state is none_after_bounded_search.
